title: OKR Weave Gate and Resource Resonance Plan
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: Company-level OKRs for 2026-Q2 were scoped independently by pillars; multiple initiatives are competing for the same constrained engineering and infra capacity (GPU pools, reliability SRE cycles, Console analytics work). Without an explicit gating and resource-resonance mechanism, we risk overcommit, missed SLAs, and reactive trade-offs mid-cycle.

Goal: Produce an operational 'Weave Gate'—a lightweight gating template + resource-resonance map that cross-links each company initiative to capacity lanes, decision owners, risk tiers, and a release gating rubric. The artifact should enable PM/Eng/Design/Finance leaders to make consistent tradeoffs at planning and to automate signals for mid-cycle rebalancing.

Deliverables:
1) Weave Gate template (YAML + Confluence playbook) with fields: initiative obj, OKR alignment, resource lanes impacted, committed capacity, fallback variant, gating window, owner, and sign-off checklist.
2) Initiative Resource Resonance Map (Miro + CSV) mapping initiatives to infra pools, SRE on-call weeks, design bandwidth, and finance runway.
3) Gating runbook and decision matrix (playbook for green/amber/red outcomes) including escalation paths and cost-latency tradeoff heuristics.
4) Prototype Console dashboard card (tokenized cost + capacity slack signal) to surface gating alerts.

Scope: Company-level initiatives only (not individual feature tickets). Work primarily with initiative owners and tech leads; integrate with Console and Finance dashboards where feasible.

Constraints & trade-offs: Keep template simple to avoid process overhead (target 15–30 minute sign-off). Full automation with Console signals is desirable but may be deferred to a follow-up sprint if engineering bandwidth is constrained. Prioritization between latency SLOs and unit-cost efficiency will require exec-level arbitration for initiatives that touch customer-facing SLAs.

Success metrics: 80% of company initiatives signed through Weave Gate before Q2 planning lock; fewer mid-cycle scope escalations compared to last quarter; first pass Console gating alerts for 3 high-risk initiatives during first 6 weeks of Q2.
acceptance_criteria: Weave Gate template published in Confluence and linked from initiative PRDs
All company-level initiatives (N >= 6) have completed the gate during Q2 planning
Resource Resonance Map contains verified capacity assignments for GPU, SRE, Design, and Finance for each initiative
Gating runbook includes clear decision owners and two escalation tiers (PM -> Eng Dir -> GTM Exec)
Prototype Console card surfaces capacity slack signal for at least 3 initiatives and emits an alert when slack < 20%

impact_summary: Implementing the Weave Gate will reduce mid-cycle resource fights and provide an auditable link between OKR commitments and capacity. Near-term impact includes clearer tradeoffs during planning and early alerts for initiatives at risk of exceeding latency or cost budgets. Long-term, this creates a feedback loop tying Console telemetry to prioritization decisions.
notes: Risk: If teams treat the gate as bureaucratic, sign-offs will be superficial. Mitigation: keep template lightweight and require one data point (capacity slack or fallback variant) per initiative.
Follow-up: If prototype Console integration is delayed, fallback to a weekly automated CSV export from capacity planning sheets.
Suggestion from Eng: Add a runway buffer field for Dedicated vs Hosted routing to handle burst capacity needs.
